newsitem.title: POLAND: Daiwa says buy Amica Wronki below PLN 60.
newsitem.headline: Daiwa says buy Amica Wronki below PLN 60.

text.p: Investors should buy shares in Polish households appliance maker Amica Wronki SA at below 60 zlotys, 10 zlotys higher than its recent IPO price, Daiwa Europe Limited said in its June Central/Eastern Europe report.

"The stock's IPO valuation rates Amica at 14.5 times on current EPS and 10.5 times on 1998 profits -- very modest in light of growth prospects and versus the Polish non-financial market PER of 15 times. The shares are a buy below 60 zlotys."

Daiwa said a successful IPO launch had provided Amica a capital injection which would help finance its investment plans for 1997-1999 and that a post-IPO debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4 times meant further expansion could be comfortably financed.
Amica Wronki's IPO of nearly 2.2 million shares was oversubscribed.
Daiwa said Amica's profit margins were double those of its key rivals and that new investment in productivity and capacity should help it ensure a cost advantage in the near future.
It said Amica's plan to more effectively penetrate appliance sub-segments and then attack CEFTA and EU markets would counter future competitive margin pressures.
Daiwa saw Amica Wronki's net profit rising to 29.8 million zlotys this year, 41.4 million zlotys next year and 56.4 million in 1999 from 25.3 million zlotys in 1996.
Price-to-earnings would rise to 14.7 this year from 11.5 last year before falling to 10.5 in 1998 and 7.8 in 1999.
Earnings per share would fall to 3.41 zlotys this year from 4.34 last year and then rise to 4.74 zlotys in 1998 and 6.45 in 1999.
Daiwa saw sales volume growth at 12 percent this year after last year's 57 percent.
